subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion intentionally break the previously supported existing-path workflow by refusing every existing directory, even a valid or empty checkout path?
rationale: Remote validation cannot establish that adopted Git state is safe, but categorical refusal is a shipped CLI workflow change that affects existing users and must be explicitly owned as the security-versus-compatibility policy.

options.title: Require a fresh path
options.body: Approve categorical refusal for unrelated existing paths, while requiring SQLite-backed retry ownership and explicit upgrade documentation before merge.

options.title: Design a compatibility migration
options.body: Preserve the user workflow by creating a sanitized sibling checkout and offering a deliberate, non-destructive migration or path switch instead of adopting the existing directory.

options.title: Pause the conversion change
options.body: Keep current behavior temporarily and close or narrow this PR until maintainers choose a durable package-to-dev migration policy.

recommendation.title: Require a fresh path
recommendation.body: Approve categorical refusal for unrelated existing paths, while requiring SQLite-backed retry ownership and explicit upgrade documentation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties the central updater orchestration, post-update handoff, and service-refresh contracts most strongly to this owner candidate.
